notes: Sealed held-out briefs for scripts/run_baseline_gate.py. Written by an independent agent on 2026-10-22 and not read by the maintainer while tuning the skill. Open them only for a release decision; once a run on these briefs has informed a change, write a new sealed set.

briefs.prompt: Design the main screen of our street parking app for Android. A driver who has just parked by the kerb wants to pay for the spot and see when their time will run out.
Design the trip screen of our airline's app for iPhone and iPhone Duo. On the day of the flight, a traveller at the airport opens it to find their gate, boarding time and seat.

Map the flow for applying to a job in our job search app, from the notification about a new job that matches a saved search to seeing that the application has been sent. The app is on iPhone, iPhone Duo and Android.
Create a UI spec for the board and card detail screens of a project management app on Android phones and foldables.

Write a UI spec for the navigation screen of our iPhone sailing app. The phone sits in a waterproof case at the helm of a small yacht, wet with spray and in bright sun, and the skipper glances at it for heading, speed and the next waypoint, one hand on the tiller.

Could you review the home screen of our iPhone hearing-aid app for usability and accessibility? At the top, two hearing-aid icons show the battery level of the left and right aid as green, amber or red, with no number. Below them, each ear has its own '-' and '+' volume buttons, 30 pt square, with each pair marked only 'L' or 'R' in light grey 12 pt text. The listening programs (Everyday, Restaurant, Music and TV) are a horizontally scrolling row of cards that show only an icon, and the active one has a thin blue outline. Muting both aids means pressing and holding the volume area, which nothing on the screen mentions. If the aids disconnect, the only sign is a short sound from the phone's speaker. No screenshot is available.

Create a typography and spacing system for our rehearsal app for theatre actors on iPhone and iPhone Duo. A script page mixes scene headings, character names, dialogue and stage directions, and an actor learning a part has to spot their own lines at a glance.

Please prepare the design rationale and developer handoff for the redesigned profile screen in our dating app. Photos used to sit in a swipeable carousel at the top; now they run down the page one after another, with the person's answers to profile prompts placed between them. Name, age and distance appear over the bottom of the first photo. Each photo and each answer has its own heart button, and a 'Pass' button stays fixed at the bottom left of the screen. The report option moved from a flag icon in the header into the overflow menu. We removed the compatibility percentage and the 'Super like' button.
